instructions: Set the oven racks in the upper and lower thirds, heat the oven to 400°F and line two baking sheets with parchment.
Scrub the sweet potatoes and dry them well. Leave the peels on and cut them into sticks about 1/4 to 1/2 inch wide and 3 inches long, keeping them even so they cook at the same speed.

Put the sticks in a big bowl, sprinkle over the cornstarch and toss until they look lightly dusted. Drizzle over the olive oil, then add 1/2 tsp of the salt, the pepper and the garlic powder and toss until every stick is coated.
Spread the fries on the two sheets in a single layer with space between them, since crowded fries steam and go soft.

Bake for 20 minutes. Flip the fries with a spatula, move any that are browning fast toward the middle, swap the pans' positions and bake for 10 to 15 minutes, until they're crisp and brown outside and soft inside.
Sprinkle with the last 1/4 tsp salt and serve right away while they're crisp.
To keep leftovers: refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days and re-crisp on a baking sheet at 350°F until hot. They won't crisp in the microwave.
method_notes: Well Plated (the lead) bakes peel-on sticks at 400°F on two sheets, flipping them halfway and swapping the pans. Its egg white is left out for a vegan snack, with an extra tablespoon of oil as the lead suggests. A tablespoon of cornstarch, which Cookie and Kate and The Forked Spoon both use for crunch, makes up for the missing egg white. Cookie and Kate bake hotter, at 425°F, with thinner sticks.
